units.sentence: Every card uses the same fields, and one rule sets every evidence label.
"Supported" means a record that settles the point backs the claim.
For what a rule says, that record is the rule's own text.
For money, needs or effects, it is a county record written by someone other than the people making the claim ...
"Uncertain" means only statements or requests by the people making the claim back it, or the key document isn't out yet.
"Not mainly a factual question" means the claim is about what is fair or right.
When a card makes more than one claim, each part gets its own label.
A claim type says "with a values question" when the card also asks what is fair or right.
"Documented" means a real person or body made the argument, and we cite where.
Cards are paired by topic: who drafts (1 and 2), openness and requests (3 and 4), then timing (5) and funding (6).
In each pair, the case for the current process comes first; the order is not a ranking.

framing_issues.text: Once submitted, the draft serves "as presented" until the Board acts.
framing_issues.issue: Same wording at lines 25, 43, 90 and 95. 'Once submitted' is not in the code and implies the commission's draft takes effect on Nov 15. A budget 'for the following year' can only operate in 2027, and only until adoption (due by the second January meeting). Used in card 1's 'What challenges it', it inflates the commission's power over the outcome.

framing_issues.text: In the 2026 cycle, the adopted General Fund was within about 0.4% of the proposal.
framing_issues.issue: Net-total comparison used as a challenge implies the draft largely fixes the result. It hides gross changes (+$20.6M on Jan 7, −$16.6M on Jan 21, a $32.17M revenue line dropped, consent decree +$18.2M), and the 2026 draft came from the county manager alone, not this commission.

framing_issues.text: dropped a proposed $32,170,000 line called "Additional Property Taxes (Consent)."
framing_issues.issue: Missing context: this was a revenue line, and in the same changes the regular Property Taxes line rose by $18,535,960 (P-054). Readers may think the Board cut taxes by $32 million or cut spending.

framing_issues.text: Who pays: Staff would have had less than four weeks ... requests beyond the plan came to about $222 million ... no money for program additions
framing_issues.issue: Option C's 'Who pays' stacks a $222 million figure and 'no money' on a resolution the page itself says 'spent no money' (line 110). This suggests listing requests has a cost. The $222 million is also only part of 2026's unmet requests, and P-031 frames the step as departments' opportunity to submit, not a staff burden.

framing_issues.text: No source gives the commission's reason for the limit, but county records show tight finances.
framing_issues.issue: Supplies a plausible motive for the limit that no source attributes to the commission, in the slot that challenges the critics; uses FY2026 records for a 2027 decision.

framing_issues.text: The code neither allows nor forbids a cap on requests.
framing_issues.issue: Settles a disputed legal question against the critics' reading (P-029 argues the cap makes the Sec. 2-261 mandate 'effectively' impossible). Line 82's 'mentions' wording is the neutral version.

framing_issues.text: Commissioner Ellis answered their objections in both news reports.
framing_issues.issue: In the Atlanta News First report Ellis 'responded to the allegation' by Commissioner Barrett (P-072, P-073), not to the justice leaders. Line 126 ('Their views, and Ellis's replies') repeats the framing, making the exchange look like a direct back-and-forth with the leaders.

framing_issues.text: The Board did not adopt that resolution.
framing_issues.issue: Placed right after the resolution's claim that the commission failed its duty, the Board's procedural disposition reads as a rebuttal of that factual claim; no record gives a reason for filing (line 120).

framing_issues.text: Barrett also said there are "some shenanigans" among board members "angling to take control of the budget process."
framing_issues.issue: Trimmed quote drops 'some of the current' (broadening the charge to 'board members') and her qualifier 'in a way that I feel is inappropriate'.

framing_issues.text: The code says they stand for "the policy priorities of the full board of commissioners."
framing_issues.issue: Supporters' card quotes the full-board purpose (P-007) but not P-013(2), which says each representative represents 'the interests and priorities of their respective district grouping', a point relevant to card 2's 'too much say' critique.
'Backs' reads as validation of rules the supporters wrote; the code is the design, not independent support for it. 'Sets out' is neutral.

framing_issues.text: Who disagrees: Resolution 26-0729 does not say the meetings were closed.
framing_issues.issue: Card 3's 'Who disagrees' slot is filled with what the critics did not say, rather than the critics' actual access objection (P-076: presenting needs 'to a two-commissioner panel rather than the full board'), which makes the critical side look like it does not disagree.
The page adopts the coalition's self-chosen name ('calling themselves "Justice Leaders"', P-076) as its neutral descriptor throughout; 'the six justice officials' would avoid adopting a side's label.

framing_issues.text: Whether the vote comes in December or January
framing_issues.issue: The code sets only a latest date; framing the choice as December or January omits that the Nov 18 meeting is not barred by the code.

framing_issues.text: Atlanta News First said it was still waiting to hear back from the vice chair
framing_issues.issue: Accurate, but singling out one official's non-response can read as evasive; acceptable here because it explains her absence from the quotes.
